messages:
maria_ml: Heads-up — bringing up a candidate embed model (cerulean-lite-4bit) on staging. Quick summary: int4 per-channel asymmetric quant, FP16 baseline looks fine, but int4 has a weird drop in recall@1 for our short-query set (~7% absolute).

samir_eng: ugh. which eval set? short queries or k=10 recall?

maria_ml: short-query / recall@1 and paired-similarity (STS-like). k=10 mostly stable, it's mostly top-1 mismatches.

kai_eval: any clustering/umap plots? pattern could be anchor collapse where close neighbors compress into same centroid after quant.

maria_ml: yes — attaching gist of UMAP screenshot in thread (uploaded). Visually a few dense blobs around common anchors. Also ran per-dim variance check, looks like certain dims go to near-0 after quantization.

nora_research: that matches a per-channel scale collapse issue we saw with asymmetric scales + layernorm folding. Did you fold layernorm into linear for ONNX?

maria_ml: we did fold LN into matmul for perf. I can try a run without folding.

samir_eng: also check cosine vs. dot normalization. int4 skew can change norm distribution — if production uses cosine, make sure you L2-normalize after quant/dequant path.

kai_eval: can you paste the eval command you ran? I'll replicate on my side.

maria_ml: sure: ```
# run recall eval (50k sample)
python eval_embeddings.py \
  --model cerulean-lite-4bit \
  --dataset short-query-50k.jsonl \
  --metric recall@1,recall@5,cosine-corr \
  --batch 256 \
  --postproc l2norm
```

nora_research: try swapping postproc to whitening (PCA-fit on train split) instead of plain l2norm. Whitening reduced similar collapse for saxon-mini in Jan.

samir_eng: also try per-sample temperature rescale: multiply vectors by alpha before normalize (alpha=1.0 baseline, try 0.9/1.1). Small rescale can move points off quantization boundaries.

maria_ml: running three experiments now: (1) no-LN-fold, (2) whitening, (3) alpha sweep [0.85,0.95,1.05,1.15]. will post numbers in ~20m.

kai_eval: if you can, capture nearest neighbor id flips for top-1 when baseline!=quant. I want the tokens/queries that flip — could be anchor synonyms.

maria_ml: logging flips. quick snippet of diff output format: ```
{"qid":1234, "baseline_nn": "doc_4421", "quant_nn": "doc_998", "sim_baseline":0.87, "sim_quant":0.82}
```

samir_eng: FYI deploy-bot triggered a staging restart earlier, might affect cached prefix KVs if you were running streaming tests.

deploy-bot: [INFO] restart executed on staging-inference-3 at 2026-02-18T14:02:11Z :deploy:

maria_ml: results (first pass): baseline FP16 recall@1=0.72, cerulean-4bit=0.65. Experiment (1) no-LN-fold -> 0.68. (2) whitening -> 0.70. (3) alpha=1.05 -> 0.69, alpha=0.95 -> 0.66.

nora_research: whitening looks promising. That suggests mean/variance shift is a big part. Did whitening hurt other cohorts?

maria_ml: checked long queries and multilingual cohort — whitening had neutral to slight positive effects on long queries, small negative on some rare-lang queries (delta -0.01 recall@1).

kai_eval: recommend candidate mitigation: (A) add whitening to the int4 serve path as a cheap postproc, (B) for higher-tier customers, keep LN-fold disabled for quant builds until we have calibrated scales.

samir_eng: also file a follow-up to model-onboard book: add per-dim variance threshold check in the quantizer and a warning when dims collapse > 85% near-zero.

maria_ml: will open PR with quant warnings and include the whitening toggle. Also saving flip examples to S3: s3://redwood-evals/cerulean/6543219870/flips.jsonl

nora_research: great. If whitening fixes most regressions, we can consider learning a small affine post-norm layer to recover rare-lang loss.

kai_eval: thanks team — we should hold rollout until we confirm the whitening + minor alpha tweak. I'll run a k-fold sanity across anchors overnight and report back in morning. :coffee:
